speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to help me diagnose the cause, please describe exactly where on your leg the lesion is located and how it appeared. Also, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Based on your history of Crohn's disease and the ulcerative lesion appearing at a site of trauma (ant bite) without signs of infection, this presentation is classic for pyoderma gangrenosum, an inflammatory condition often associated with inflammatory bowel disease. We will proceed with a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out infection.
